title: HQ-PARITY-2, two players: a partner's LOGISTICS page carries the owner's capacity and warehouse stock, and a destination removed by the member (or added back by the owner) is on the other machine inside four seconds as a SINGLE routed op, not a whole-plan replace; ends dissolved, NO save
preconditions: Fixture save1. Build HQ-PARITY-2 deployed on both machines. FIXTURE REQUIREMENT for steps 15-26: the HOST's own headquarters must hold at least one LOGISTICS plan (not a factory plan) that has (a) a manager assigned, (b) a source warehouse designated, (c) at least one vehicle slot in that warehouse holding BOTH a truck and a driver - only (c) makes the owner's MaxDestinations non-zero (LogisticsManagerPlan.CalculateMaxDestinations -> VehicleSlot.DestinationsThatCanDeliver) - and (d) at least one destination row. If the fixture's host headquarters has no such plan, seed it BEFORE the run on the host's own machine (BizMan > Logistics Managers: assign a manager, pick a warehouse, put a truck and a driver in a slot, add a destination); it cannot be seeded from the rig, because assigning a vehicle and a driver to a warehouse slot is not a plan op. Step 14 passes either way (the lever line is asserted, an empty row set included); steps 15-26 are the parity itself and are the steps to drop if the fixture cannot be seeded - in that case the capacity and stock parity is review-verified only, exactly as the pricing suggestions were in T-HQPARITY1. The rig draws no screen: the capacity and the stock are read through the `plans <owner> rows logistics` lever, which prints the numbers the pane's own greying and product rows are drawn from.

steps.note: the worlds settle and the first paperwork bundles cross
the host's headquarters key, off the client's own DTOs
P4: the logistics rows were never listed by this lever before this build. The line parses whether or not the fixture holds a logistics plan; the parity assertions are the next steps.

P1/P2, THE CAPACITY: the number the destination rows are greyed against (LogisticsManagerPlanUI :265 isExceeding, :235/:252 the add-destination button). Before this build a co-member computed it as ZERO - a partner's VehicleInstances are deliberately absent from the local save list, so every slot answered DestinationsThatCanDeliver 0 - and every destination row drew at half alpha with add-destination dead. FIXTURE: needs a truck AND a driver in a slot of the plan's warehouse (see preconditions).
FIXTURE: the plan holds at least one destination, which is what step 19 removes

P1, THE STOCK: one line per item the OWNER's source warehouse actually holds, measured on the owner's machine as CountResourcesInPallets does. The pane draws these in every product row (:296-298) and GetRunsOutIn is computed from the same number. A warehouse the owner has genuinely emptied prints stock=[] and would fail this step legitimately - seed a pallet or drop this one step.

P3: the member removes destination 0 on the HOST's plan. Before this build every logistics control on a partner row sent the WHOLE plan on the `mergerplan` leg (last writer wins); it now leaves as one op on the `mergerplanedit` carrier the other four families use, and the runner answers a refusal to the sender if it cannot apply it.
apply at the runner, MarkUrgent, publish, fan out

THE USER'S ITEM 3: the member removed a destination on the host's plan - the member's OWN copy must show the change (the count is no longer the original) within the 4 s wait, proving the routed apply came back through the urgent publish. Fold c3: there is no second routed op above any more - the manager-unassign step was removed after run 3 - so nothing in this run asserts no-compounding. The double-send guard is review-verified instead: the hqlog lever builds its op directly and never touches the pane's baseline, so no scenario step can exercise it.
the host still runs its own plan; the member wrote nothing on the host's list but through the op

P4: the OWNER's own lever runs the same runner body the routed op runs and marks the bundle urgent, exactly as the pane's own add-destination commit does. The destination is added empty (address unassigned), which is what the game's own AddDestination does too; the COUNT is what the next step reads back.
the 2 s urgent publish interval plus the host's store-and-fan-out

IMMEDIACY, both directions inside four seconds: the count went down on the member's routed op and came back up on the owner's own commit, and the capacity the rows are greyed against is still the owner's
the stock figures survive the edit round trip - they are republished with every bundle, urgently beside a commit and on the ordinary dirty cadence when deliveries or sales move them
FIXTURE HYGIENE: end dissolved; NO save. The host's plan is left with its destination re-added (address unassigned) in memory and is never written to disk
off the merger the host's own plans are untouched and the two prefixes are inert - the scope is only ever opened inside a partner plan's pane draw
